fun_highlights: The vocation x era intersection cards (vx_*) genuinely create combinations a completionist hunts for. 'vx_scholar_turning' and 'vx_soldier_war' exist only when a specific calling meets a specific historical moment — a completionist who has seen 30 lives will still be looking for all 3 such intersections, and the prose in each is distinct enough to reward finding it.

The callback chain depth is real and satisfying. The 'child_books' thread — picked up at age 7-12 (c_book), resurfacing as 'cb_books_late' in midlife to re-read or pass on, and then optionally inherited by the heir as a latent memory — is a three-generation arc that a completionist can recognise and feel the closure of. The 'looked_away' / 'cb_lookaway' callback works similarly.

Dynasty-state gating creates genuinely exclusive content. 'dyn_summit', 'dyn_decline', and 'dyn_founder_echo' are unreachable in the first three generations. 'dyn_decline' especially — requiring gen>=4, seat<=2, AND peakSeat>=4 — is the kind of combinatorially specific condition that a long player will eventually hit and experience as a discovery.

The fate cards (f_fire, f_sudden_loss, f_grace, f_reversal) with no 'no' option are a structural surprise. Most cards offer escape; these simply land. 'f_grace' in particular has only one choice ('Take it, and pass it on someday') and that single-option grammar signals something different happened to this life. The once-per-dynasty-6 cooldown on f_grace means a long session may see it 2-3 times across 15 dynasties, keeping it genuinely rare.

The trait-affinity weighting on childhood cards (engine.js lines 281-283) is invisible but effective. A bookish child leans toward c_book, a restless one toward c_steal and c_move. Across 15 dynasties the transcripts show this is actually working — Aldous Renner (bright, stubborn) shrugs at wonder and takes the world as it comes; Soren Castellane (dreaming) leans into books and love. Childhoods are not identical.

The 'adrift' vocation as a distinct fifth arc is properly implemented, not a stub. 'y_adrift', 'a_adrift_work', 'm_adrift_reckon', and 'e_adrift_old' form a coherent parallel to the four called arcs. Dynasty 11, Calla Okonkwo's life (deliberately drifting, making peace with it, final tally of 'doors a fixed life would have opened') reads as a complete, characteristically different arc — a completionist who has seen many soldier and scholar lives will find this genuinely fresh.
staleness: The body-decline observation pool fires identically across lives regardless of character. In the transcripts, 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them' (Dynasty 1, Iris), 'Her legs know something the rest of her is not yet ready to hear' (Dynasty 11, Calla Okonkwo), 'The stairs have started to ask a question of him' (Dynasty 6, Idris Salvedi) all arrive in the same mid-50s window with the same weight. The engine.js observe() pools are large (10 lines each) but use firedObs — so each LIFE gets only one. Across a 15-dynasty session the freshPick deduplification isn't across dynasties, only within a life, so a completionist will see 'the stairs' line multiple times in a single sitting.

The 'teach or guard knowledge' binary (m_scholar_legacy) and its outcome lines land in nearly every scholar life with near-identical prose. Dynasty 1 Iris: 'Gave away everything she knew, freely and to anyone who'd take it, and so made sure it outlived her.' Dynasty 2 Tobias: exact same line. Dynasty 3 Greta Ashby Cassian: exact same line again. The content.js freshPick pool for 'became_teacher' has only two variants for the 'Give it all away' branch, and the cooldown (3 generations for onceDyn) means it will rotate back. For a completionist playing many scholarly houses, this is the single most-seen exact repeated sentence.

The founding-circumstance opener (c_origin) keys on era and seat with 7 prose branches, but 8 of the 15 transcripts open in 'settled' era with seat 1-2, triggering the same three-item freshPick pool ('earliest years pass the way most do...'). Dynasty 1 Carys, Dynasty 9 Anders Sereno, Dynasty 14 Niall Marchetti, and Dynasty 7 Junia Calloway all draw from the same fallback pool. The early-life atmosphere is the reader's first impression each dynasty — identical openings in more than half of runs collapses the sense that each house begins somewhere distinct.

The 'bequest' card (e_bequest) fires in almost every life with children, and its four choices produce nearly the same body-of-chronicle effect regardless of which is chosen. In the transcripts: Dynasty 1 Carys chooses 'The stories, and the warmth'; Dynasty 1 Ronja, Dynasty 6 Linnea Salvedi, Dynasty 11 Yara all choose 'Nothing but their own freedom'; Dynasty 2 Edmund/Tobias choose 'mind' or 'means'. The heir-screen BEQ_LINE text ('From [name], deliberately: everything they knew — a mind with a running start') is distinct, but a completionist playing many 5-generation dynasties will see e_bequest fire predictably in the late 60s every single time. The timing is not varied — the age window is 60-95 with w:5 and once:true, making it essentially guaranteed.

The 'from nothing' structural beat (s_from_nothing) and the 'invest in the name' beat (m_invest_name) create a visible backbone that every dynasty of low or medium standing follows in roughly the same order: found -> struggle -> 'begin from nothing' -> 'invest the name' -> motto crystallizes. Looking at dynasties 1 through 6 in the transcripts, the structural arc of a rising house is legible and repetitive at the mid-level beats even as the surface prose rotates. The 'self_made' / 'built_the_name' memory-flag path through reputation -> motto is too reliable; a completionist who has built three scholarly houses and two industrious ones will find the fourth and fifth feel like re-runs of the same procedural.

The solitary-life elder cards (m_solitary, e_solitary) share outcome prose with the wanderer-life elder cards in ways that flatten what should be distinct shapes. Dynasty 1 Ronja: 'Sat, at the last, with the plain ache of an unshared life, and let it be exactly the size it was.' Dynasty 11 Calla Okonkwo: same card, same choice, same prose. These are lives with completely different backstories (restless wanderer vs deliberate drifter) but the elder shape converges on the same closing beat. For a completionist who reads chronicles closely, the lack of vocation-sensitivity in solitary/elder cards is a missed texture.

improvements.what: Add a dynasty-level deduplication pass for the observe() pool lines, not just per-life. Currently firedObs is reset per life (engine.js), so 'the stairs' and 'each day asks a little more' can recur verbatim across nearby lives in the same session. A RECENT_OBS array analogous to RECENT_LINES (dynasty.js) — blocking the last N used observation strings from the session pool — would eliminate the most visible repeated ambient lines.
improvements.why: Observation lines are background texture that the reader absorbs semi-consciously. Seeing 'the stairs have started to ask a question of them' in dynasty 1 and dynasty 6 erodes the sense that each life is its own. The fix is low-touch (the infrastructure already exists in RECENT_LINES) and high-reward for a completionist reading chronicles back to back.

improvements.what: Split the 'm_scholar_legacy' 'give it away' log line into at least 4-6 distinct variants instead of the current 2, and apply an onceDyn:5 cooldown to prevent the same variant appearing within 5 generations. Currently: only 'Gave away everything they knew, freely and to anyone who'd take it, and so made sure it outlived them' and two alternates — insufficient for a completionist who builds scholarly houses sequentially.
improvements.why: This is the single most-repeated exact sentence in the 15-dynasty transcripts. It appears verbatim in Dynasty 1 (Iris), Dynasty 2 (Tobias), Dynasty 8 (Cassian), Dynasty 9 (Anders Sereno), Dynasty 14 (Niall) — five times in 15 dynasties. The 'teacher' epitaph cluster is also block-protected at 3, so the life-ending beat rotates, but the mid-life beat that earns it does not.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 era-specific and seat-specific variants to the c_origin fallback pool for 'settled' era at low seat, so the most common opening (8 of 15 dynasties) diverges. Current fallback is a 3-item pool shared by every ordinary founder in an ordinary time. At minimum: add a variant each for gen>=3 (born into a story already underway — distinct from the gen>=5 path which exists), for a sibling in the house, and for traits like 'guarded' or 'frail' that currently have no opener flavoring.
improvements.why: The first lines of a life set the register. When more than half of dynasty openers pull from the same 3-item pool, the game announces 'this is a normal start' before a word of choice is made — erasing the era and trait variation the engine works to build over subsequent cards.

improvements.what: Add vocation-sensitivity to the solitary (m_solitary, e_solitary) and childless (e_childless) elder cards. A wanderer who has been solitary by choice should get different prose from a maker who never found love; a scholar who stayed childless to pursue the question should frame their elder reckoning in terms of what the work leaves, not the generic 'unshared life' framing. Currently these cards are entirely vocation-blind.
improvements.why: Vocations gate distinct adult and elder arcs for called lives but the solitary/childless shapes — which now account for roughly a quarter and a seventh of lives by design — collapse into the same generic elder voice regardless of who the person was. A completionist who has seen 8+ solitary endings will find them undifferentiated.

improvements.what: Give the 'plague' era its own vocation x era card (vx_healer_plague or vx_scholar_plague) parallel to vx_scholar_turning and vx_soldier_war. Currently plague provides w_plague_tend as a universal fate card, but a scholar or maker in a plague era faces no vocation-coloured intersection — only the same tend-or-distance binary that a wanderer faces. The existing w_plague_tend already sets a single-option-style pressure; an additional vx card for the knowledge professions (do you use your learning to understand the sickness, or bury yourself in work to avoid it?) would add a genuinely new intersection for a completionist hunting vocation-era content.
improvements.why: The three existing vx_ cards are among the most distinctive content in the game (per the highlights). Plague is the one era with no vx entry, which a completionist will notice as a gap after finding the scholar-turning and soldier-war intersections.

verdict: A Life has genuine depth beneath the surface — the callback chains, dynasty-state gates, and vocation-arc structure give a completionist real things to find and reason to keep playing across many dynasties. The staleness problem is real but narrower than it looks: the specific failure is a cluster of roughly a dozen phrases (the 'teach everything' scholar lines, the 'stairs' observation, the solitary elder coda) that rotate slowly enough to appear verbatim in three or four houses out of fifteen. For a completionist reading chronicles back to back, these exact repetitions are the principal brake on the sense of discovery — not structural sameness, which the engine manages reasonably well, but literal repeated sentences that should be easy to fix. Score 6.9: a strong foundation with a small number of high-visibility staleness failures concentrated in scholar-life beats and observation-line recycling.
